newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger, yield curve flattens.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger, yield curve flattens.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Tuesday, boosted by a firmer U.S. market, with the yield curve flattening on concern the Bank of Canada would not cut interest rates again soon, analysts said.

"The feeling right now is this could be the last Bank of Canada rate cut," said Sheldon Dong, manager of fixed income research with Midland Walwyn. "The yield curve is historically steep, so people are doing term extension trades."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.58 to C$115.95 to yield 6.705 percent, while the U.S. 30-year benchmark bonds rose 26/32 to yield 6.45 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 26 basis points from 24 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

Canada's central bank made it 11th short term rate cut this year on Friday, bringing its key bank rate down to 3.25 percent, the lowest since the early 1960's. Today's weekly government T-bill auction saw the yield on the three-month T-bill fall to its lowest since 1961.

The easing by the Bank has resulted in a historically steep yield curve. With expectations waning that rates will be cut further, investors are moving up the curve in search of higher yields and better value, analysts said.
"They're saying we've basically wrung out as much as we can by being in the short end, let's move up the curve a bit," said Dong.
Otherwise, Canadian bonds benefitted from further strength and technical momentum in U.S. Treasuries, analysts said.

Dealers said investors are now looking ahead to tomorrow's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee. The committee is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged. Investors are also awaiting Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen's semi-annual monetary policy report on Thursday.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.20 to C$106.45 to yield 6.130 percent. The U.S. 10-year rose 15/32 to yield 6.19 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to six basis points from 12 basis points at Monday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.88 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.17 percent.
